tasks.prompt: Order a force main detention and sulfide generation review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sulfide problems at a discharge worsened after flows fell, and detention time in the force main is suspected to have increased.

cards.label: Compare the current detention times with the detention at design flows and with the period when sulfide complaints began
Review the pump cycling and any operational changes that leave sewage standing in the main between cycles
Adopt the change if the trial reduces sulfide, or refer the reach to the chemical dosing or ventilation program with the evidence
Trial the selected operational change and monitor sulfide and odour at the discharge through the trial
Identify operational options that shorten detention, such as revised pump sequencing or more frequent shorter runs
Calculate the force main volume from its diameter and length and the detention time at current average and low flows

tasks.explanation: Detention is calculated from real volumes and flows before operations are blamed. A monitored trial decides adoption, and referral to dosing is made on evidence when operations cannot fix it.

tasks.prompt: Order a corrosion inspection program for concrete collection structures.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crown corrosion is suspected in trunk sewers and manholes downstream of force main discharges and low ventilation reaches.

cards.label: Choose the inspection method for each structure, from manhole condition assessment to CCTV with sonar or laser profiling for large trunks
Set the reinspection interval for monitored structures based on the corrosion rate found
Carry out the inspections and record the remaining wall, the depth of corrosion, and the structural condition in the standard grading
Rank the structures for lining, repair, or monitoring and enter the ranked list into the rehabilitation program
Select the structures for inspection from the sulfide monitoring results, age, material, and the consequence of a collapse or failure
Estimate the remaining service life for each inspected structure using the measured corrosion and the observed rate indicators

tasks.explanation: Sulfide evidence and consequence select the structures, and measured remaining wall drives the life estimate. Ranked actions feed rehabilitation, and monitored structures get a reinspection date tied to the rate found.

tasks.prompt: Order the commissioning of a lift station odour control unit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a carbon adsorption unit has been installed at a station with persistent odour complaints from nearby homes.

cards.label: Measure the airflow at the unit and confirm it matches the design ventilation rate for the spaces served
Set the operating schedule, media condition checks, and the alarm or inspection routine in the station procedures
Brief the station operators on media life indicators and the work order route for media replacement
Run the unit and measure hydrogen sulfide and odour indications at the inlet and outlet to confirm removal performance
Verify the installation against the design, including ducting, fan rotation, damper positions, and the foul air capture at the wet well and screen area
Record the commissioning results and set a complaint review after three months to confirm the neighbourhood impact has fallen

tasks.explanation: Installation and airflow are verified before performance is measured, because poor capture defeats good media. Operators are briefed on media life, and the complaint review judges success where it matters.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning of a ventilation upgrade for a corrosion damaged trunk reach.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk sewer reach with high sulfide and crown corrosion will receive forced ventilation with treatment at the discharge point.

cards.label: Stage the project in the capital plan with commissioning measurements defined in advance
Evaluate the ventilation rate options and the treatment methods against the objective and the measured sulfide load
Select the preferred arrangement and confirm it does not push foul air to untreated openings elsewhere in the reach
Survey the reach for ventilation access points, power availability, and a treatment location that neighbours can accept
Define the post project monitoring that will prove the corrosion and odour benefit and report it to the odour program
Confirm the ventilation objective for the reach, covering corrosion control, odour control, or both, using the monitoring evidence

tasks.explanation: The objective is set from evidence before rates and methods are compared. Checking that foul air is not simply moved protects other neighbourhoods, and post project monitoring is defined before construction, not after.

tasks.prompt: Order the prioritization of sulfide corrosion mitigation in the capital plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inspection and monitoring have identified nine reaches and structures needing corrosion mitigation over ten years.

cards.label: Assemble the condition, remaining life, and consequence of failure for each candidate reach and structure
Present the sequenced program with the risk it retires each year for capital approval
Sequence the ranked work so upstream sulfide controls that protect several downstream assets are credited for their full benefit
Estimate the mitigation cost and the life extension for each option, including lining, ventilation, and dosing based controls
Rank the candidates by risk reduction for the cost and by how soon the remaining life expires
Review the sequence after each inspection cycle and promote any asset whose corrosion is advancing faster than estimated

tasks.explanation: Ranking uses remaining life and consequence together, because a cheap fix on an asset with decades of life retires little risk. Upstream controls are credited downstream, and inspection cycles can promote assets whose corrosion accelerates.

tasks.prompt: Order a seasonal odour management plan for the summer period.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: odour complaints peak from June to September when temperatures raise sulfide generation and residents are outdoors.

cards.label: Brief customer service and field staff on the summer response standard for odour calls, including same day inspection at repeat locations
Complete an end of season review and carry the lessons into the next year plan and the capital or maintenance programs
Schedule the preventive actions before June, including wet well cleaning, air valve service, and dosing system checks at the listed locations
Set the summer operating adjustments, such as dosing rate reviews and ventilation checks, with the dates each takes effect
Track complaints and sulfide readings weekly through the summer and escalate locations that exceed the action level
Review the previous summer complaint and monitoring record and list the locations and operations that drove the peak

tasks.explanation: The plan is built from the previous summer evidence and preventive work is finished before the season starts. Weekly tracking allows escalation while the season is still running, not after it ends.

tasks.prompt: Order the optimization review of an established sulfide dosing program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a dosing system has run for two years at a fixed rate and chemical costs have risen while discharge sulfide varies with season.

cards.label: Adopt the seasonal schedule in the operating procedure with the monitoring that guards the target
Monitor the discharge closely through the first seasonal change and hold the trial rate only while the target is met
Relate the sulfide results to temperature, flow, and detention to find the periods when the fixed dose was more than needed
Calculate the chemical saving and confirm no increase in corrosion indicators at downstream structures
Compile the dosing records, chemical use, and discharge sulfide results by month for the two years of operation
Trial a seasonal dosing schedule with rates set for the high and low generation periods

tasks.explanation: Two years of records show where the fixed dose was wasted. The seasonal trial is guarded by close monitoring and corrosion checks, so savings are never bought with asset damage.

tasks.prompt: Order the setup of a fats, oils and grease program with interceptor requirements.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the municipality will require grease interceptors at food service establishments under its sewer use bylaw.

cards.label: Provide a guidance package and a pre installation contact for establishments planning the work
Begin the routine maintenance verification cycle for all registered interceptors once the compliance date passes
Notify establishments of the requirements, the compliance timeline, and the approved sizing method in writing
Inspect installations as they are completed and record each interceptor in the program registry
Build the inventory of food service establishments from business licences and health inspection records
Confirm the bylaw authority, the establishments covered, and the interceptor sizing and maintenance standard the program will enforce

tasks.explanation: Authority and standards come before the inventory, and the inventory before notification. Installations are inspected into a registry, which is what makes later maintenance verification possible.

tasks.prompt: Order a food service establishment inspection program for grease control.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 240 establishments are registered and inspections must verify interceptor condition and maintenance records.

cards.label: Inspect the highest ranked establishments, checking interceptor baffles, grease depth, and the maintenance records on site
Report inspection completion and failure patterns quarterly and adjust the ranking factors from the patterns found
Rank the establishments for inspection using blockage history downstream, establishment type, and time since the last inspection
Train inspectors on the standard inspection form, the pass and fail criteria, and the photographic record required
Issue correction notices with deadlines for failed inspections and record the required actions in the registry
Reinspect corrected establishments and close or escalate each file based on the reinspection result

tasks.explanation: Ranking sends inspectors first where blockages say the risk is. Standard forms and criteria keep inspections consistent, and quarterly pattern review improves the ranking itself.

tasks.prompt: Order the optimization of cleaning frequency for fats, oils and grease hotspots.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 18 sewer reaches are cleaned on fixed cycles for grease and several still block between cleanings while others are found nearly clean.

cards.label: Shorten the cycle for reaches that block or refill quickly and lengthen it where repeated cleanings find little grease
Link each hotspot to the upstream food service inspections so source control is checked before cleaning is intensified further
Lock the proven cycles into the maintenance plan and review hotspot status annually
Compile the blockage and cleaning records for each hotspot, including the grease depth found at each cleaning
Run the revised cycles for two quarters and compare blockages and grease findings with the previous pattern
Rank the hotspots by blockage frequency and by how fast grease reaccumulates between cleanings

tasks.explanation: Records of what cleaning actually finds drive the new cycles. Source control upstream is checked before cleaning is intensified, because cleaning treats the symptom while interceptors treat the cause.

tasks.prompt: Order an interceptor maintenance verification program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: registered establishments must pump their interceptors on schedule and the utility will verify it rather than rely on self reporting alone.

cards.label: Notify establishments of the records they must keep and the manifest information the utility will accept
Apply the compliance steps, from education to bylaw enforcement, based on the measured condition and the records
Visit the flagged establishments and measure the grease and solids depth in the interceptor
Set the verification method, covering maintenance records, hauler manifests, and the grease depth checks done during inspections
Collect and review the records for the first cycle and flag establishments with missing or implausible maintenance
Report the verification results and update the inspection ranking with the compliance history

tasks.explanation: The method and the record standard are set before establishments are judged against them. Field measurement decides the flagged cases, and compliance history feeds back into inspection ranking.

tasks.prompt: Order a fats, oils and grease public education campaign.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: residential grease is a major contributor in two neighbourhoods with repeated grease blockages in small diameter sewers.

cards.label: Coordinate with the cleaning program so hotspot cleaning in the target areas is visible during the campaign period
Confirm the target neighbourhoods from blockage records and the message that matches the behaviour found, such as pouring cooking oil into sinks
Report the campaign results and decide whether to extend, revise, or retire the campaign based on the blockage trend
Design the campaign materials with simple disposal instructions and the locations of household hazardous waste or oil drop off options
Deliver the campaign through the channels the neighbourhoods actually use, timed before the high cooking seasons
Track blockage reports in the target areas against the same period in previous years

tasks.explanation: The message is built from the behaviour behind the blockages, not from a generic script. Blockage trends in the target areas, not material counts, judge whether the campaign worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the enforcement escalation workflow for a repeat grease bylaw offender.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a food service establishment has failed two inspections, missed a correction deadline, and a grease blockage occurred downstream.

cards.label: Proceed with the bylaw charges or orders if the plan is not met, with the file evidence prepared for the process
Meet the owner to agree a written correction plan with dates if the owner engages before the deadline
Verify the file is complete, with inspection reports, photographs, notices, and the downstream blockage record documented
Issue the final notice that states the outstanding corrections, the deadline, and the charges or orders that follow non compliance
Reinspect on the plan dates and record compliance or continued failure for each required action
Keep the establishment on the frequent inspection list until it completes a full year of compliant inspections

tasks.explanation: Escalation rests on a complete evidence file. A written plan gives an engaged owner a fair path, charges follow a missed plan, and a year of compliance is required before the establishment leaves the frequent list.

tasks.prompt: Order a grease blockage root cause investigation for a repeat location.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a sewer reach has blocked with grease four times in a year despite being on a six month cleaning cycle.

cards.label: Review the blockage records and confirm the material removed each time and the exact location within the reach
Monitor the reach for a year and report whether the blockage rate fell, keeping the case open until it does
Match the findings to decide whether the driver is structural, source loading, or an inadequate cleaning method
Inspect the reach by CCTV for sags, offset joints, or low slope sections where grease can accumulate even with normal flows
Apply the matched correction, such as a structural repair, source enforcement, or a changed cleaning method and cycle
Survey the upstream establishments and residential sources and check their interceptor and disposal status

tasks.explanation: The investigation separates structure, sources, and cleaning method, because each has a different fix. The case stays open until a year of monitoring shows the blockage rate actually fell.

tasks.prompt: Order the effectiveness review of the fats, oils and grease program after two years.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the program has an interceptor registry, inspections, and hotspot cleaning, and management needs to know if blockages are falling.

cards.label: Identify the program elements with the weakest compliance or the weakest blockage response
Compile program activity, including inspections completed, compliance rates, and hotspot cleaning delivered
Revise the program plan, shifting effort toward the elements and areas the evidence supports
Report the review to management with the revised targets for the next two years
Compile grease related blockages and overflows for the two program years and the two years before the program
Compare blockage trends in the areas with full program coverage against areas not yet fully covered

tasks.explanation: Activity alone proves nothing, so blockages are compared before and after and between covered and uncovered areas. The revision shifts effort to what the comparison supports.

tasks.prompt: Order the design of a residential fats, oils and grease program for a new subdivision area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a growing area of restaurants and homes is tributary to a small lift station already showing grease fouling of floats.

cards.label: Confirm the grease sources in the tributary area, separating food service establishments from residential contributions
Add the lift station to the fouling watch list with increased float cleaning and grease checks until source controls take effect
Report the area results after a year and fold the successful elements into the systemwide program
Design the residential element, covering disposal guidance at move in, community drop off events, and reminders through utility billing
Apply the interceptor program to the establishments first, since their loads are the largest and the most controllable
Track float fouling incidents and grease blockages in the area quarterly against the starting baseline

tasks.explanation: Establishments are controlled first because their loads dominate. The station is protected more actively in the meantime, and a year of tracked results decides what joins the systemwide program.

tasks.prompt: Order a grease hauler manifest and disposal tracking program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility will track interceptor pump outs through hauler manifests to verify maintenance and lawful disposal.

cards.label: Define the manifest information required, including establishment, interceptor size, volume removed, hauler, and disposal location
Flag establishments whose manifests are missing, late, or inconsistent with their interceptor size
Collect the manifests on the set cycle and match them against the interceptor registry and the required pump out frequency
Register the haulers serving the municipality and brief them on the manifest and submission requirements
Verify a sample of manifests with the receiving disposal facility records
Use the verified data in the maintenance verification program and report hauler compliance annually

tasks.explanation: The manifest standard is defined before haulers are asked to follow it. Matching manifests to the registry finds the gaps, and sample verification with disposal facilities keeps the paper honest.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning of an annual CCTV inspection program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: about 60 km of sewer per year will be inspected, prioritized from age, material, blockage history, and rehabilitation needs.

cards.label: Confirm the cleaning required before inspection and schedule cleaning ahead of the CCTV crews so camera time is not wasted
Report the kilometres completed, the condition picture gained, and the backlog remaining at year end
Select the reaches for each objective from the asset data and record why each reach was chosen
Set the inspection objectives for the year, balancing condition assessment for capital planning with pre rehabilitation surveys and blockage investigations
Carry out the inspections to the standard defect coding and confirm daily that files, reports, and video are received and readable
Review the coded results and route structural defects to rehabilitation planning and maintenance defects to the cleaning or repair programs

tasks.explanation: Objectives decide which reaches are chosen, and cleaning precedes cameras because a dirty pipe cannot be graded. Daily file checks protect the record, and results are routed the same year they are gathered.

tasks.prompt: Order the prioritization workflow from CCTV condition results to a rehabilitation candidate list.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: three years of CCTV results cover 180 km and the rehabilitation budget can address about 6 km per year.

cards.label: Group the top ranked reaches into constructible projects by area and method
Combine likelihood and consequence into a ranked candidate list and check the top ranks against field knowledge of the reaches
Present the ranked projects for capital programming with the risk each project retires
Score each reach for structural condition, infiltration severity, and maintenance history from the verified results
Apply the consequence of failure for each reach, covering size, depth, location, and what an overflow or collapse would affect
Verify the inspection data quality and regrade or exclude inspections with poor visibility or incomplete coding

tasks.explanation: Ungradable inspections are excluded before scoring, so the ranking rests on evidence. Consequence turns a condition list into a risk list, and grouping turns the list into projects that can actually be built.

tasks.prompt: Order the delivery sequence for a cured in place pipe lining project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 800 m of trunk sewer will be lined, with flows maintained by bypass pumping during installation.

cards.label: Reinstate the laterals, restore the site, and file the warranty and asset records for the renewed reach
Confirm the pre lining CCTV, measurements, and host pipe condition support lining and finalize the liner design inputs
Plan the bypass pumping, traffic control, and resident notification for the installation window
Clean the reach and complete the pre installation CCTV immediately before the lining dates
Complete the post lining CCTV and the required testing and compare the results with the acceptance criteria
Install and cure the liner under the specified quality controls, recording temperatures, pressures, and cure times

tasks.explanation: Design inputs are confirmed before the bypass and notifications are planned around a date. Cleaning and pre CCTV come immediately before installation, and acceptance testing plus records close the renewal.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning of a pipe bursting project to upsize a capacity limited sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a 300 mm sewer at capacity will be replaced by a 450 mm pipe by pipe bursting along the same alignment.

cards.label: Design the launch and receive pits, the bypass pumping, and the service reconnection plan with the affected properties notified
Survey the alignment for utilities, laterals, and structures and confirm the bursting method suits the soil and the neighbouring services
Complete the post construction CCTV and flow check and update the asset and capacity records with the new pipe
Reconnect the laterals and structures and confirm each service is live by testing or inspection
Confirm the capacity need and the new size from the capacity assessment and the growth forecast for the tributary area
Burst the new pipe in planned pulls and record the pull forces and any ground movement observations

tasks.explanation: The size comes from the capacity assessment, and the alignment survey protects neighbouring utilities. Services are proven live after reconnection, and the capacity record is updated so the next application sees the new limit.

tasks.prompt: Order a manhole rehabilitation program for structurally deteriorated manholes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inspections found 120 manholes with structural or infiltration defects needing rehabilitation over three years.

cards.label: Complete the work with quality checks on surface preparation and thickness or bond as the method requires
Package the ranked work by basin so crews and contractors complete whole areas in one mobilization
Reinspect a sample of completed manholes and enter the renewed condition into the asset record
Match each group to a rehabilitation method, such as structural lining, cementitious coating, benching repair, or frame and cover renewal
Group the defective manholes by defect type and severity from the inspection scores and photographs
Rank the groups by safety risk, infiltration contribution, and the consequence of a structural failure

tasks.explanation: Method follows defect type, and ranking follows risk. Basin packaging reduces mobilization waste, and sample reinspection plus asset updates prove the program renewed what it paid for.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning of a lateral rehabilitation program for root and infiltration defects.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: CCTV from the main and from launch inspections shows many laterals with root intrusion and joint infiltration in one older basin.

cards.label: Notify the owners in the first phase area with the defect evidence, the options, and the program timeline
Decide the responsibility split and any cost sharing between the municipality and owners under the applicable policy and bylaw
Schedule the lining or renewal work street by street with the mainline work where both are planned
Inspect each completed lateral repair and record the renewed condition against the property record
Measure the basin infiltration change after the phase and report it to the infiltration and inflow program
Confirm the lateral defect population from the mainline and lateral inspection records and group properties by defect type

tasks.explanation: The defect population and the responsibility split are settled before owners are notified. Street by street scheduling coordinates with mainline work, and basin flow measurement judges the phase.

tasks.prompt: Order the method selection process for rehabilitating a deteriorated trunk sewer reach.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a 600 mm trunk reach has severe corrosion and infiltration and several rehabilitation methods are candidates.

cards.label: Compare the methods on capacity impact, bypass difficulty, service disruption, life extension, and whole life cost
Check the shortlisted methods against site constraints, including access, depth, and connections to structures
Select the method with engineering and operations agreement and record the reasons the alternatives were rejected
Carry the selected method, its cost, and its design requirements into the capital project definition
List the feasible methods for the reach, such as cured in place lining, sliplining, segmental repair, or open cut replacement
Assemble the condition evidence, including CCTV, corrosion measurements, flow data, and the remaining life estimate

tasks.explanation: Evidence and remaining life come before method comparison. Site constraints can defeat a paper winner, so they are checked before selection, and the rejected alternatives are documented for the record.

tasks.prompt: Order the acceptance workflow for a completed sewer rehabilitation project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a contractor has completed lining and manhole work on a project and the utility must accept or reject the work before payment.

cards.label: Enter the renewed assets, warranties, and inspection records into the asset management system
Inspect the post construction CCTV against the acceptance criteria for wrinkles, fins, infiltration, and lateral reinstatement
Reinspect the corrected work and confirm every deficiency is closed before recommending final payment
Verify the field test results and the material or cure records submitted for the installed work
Review the contract requirements and list the acceptance evidence, including post construction CCTV, test results, and as built records
Issue a deficiency list with correction deadlines for any work that fails the criteria

tasks.explanation: Acceptance evidence is defined from the contract before the CCTV is judged. Deficiencies are corrected and reinspected before final payment, and the asset records are updated so the renewal starts its tracked life.

tasks.prompt: Order the prioritization of an emergency structural repair found by CCTV.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a routine inspection finds a deformed and cracked sewer under a major road with soil visible through the defects.

cards.label: Design the permanent repair method and schedule it ahead of programmed work, displacing lower risk projects
Secure the location with traffic control or load restrictions if the road surface or the pipe is at immediate risk
Have the defect reviewed by engineering the same day to confirm the failure risk and the repair urgency
Review whether similar pipes of the same age and material need accelerated inspection and adjust the CCTV program
Complete the repair and the post repair CCTV and record the failure mode in the asset history
Decide the interim protection, such as flow monitoring, a temporary liner, or a planned bypass on standby

tasks.explanation: Public safety at the surface comes before engineering review, and interim protection bridges the time to a permanent repair. The failure mode feeds back into the inspection program for similar pipes.

tasks.prompt: Order the design review sequence for a trenchless rehabilitation project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: engineering has produced a 60 percent design for lining a trunk sewer with two lift station connections.

cards.label: Review the design flows and bypass plan against the measured flows and the station operating records
Review the liner design inputs, including host pipe condition, groundwater, and the structural class selected
Resolve the review comments with the designer and record the accepted changes in the design file
Approve the design for tender with the operations sign off recorded
Confirm the quality requirements in the specification, including CCTV acceptance, testing, and warranty terms
Check the construction sequence for service impacts, odour control, and the protection of the watercourse at the work sites

tasks.explanation: Operations review starts with flows and bypass, because construction fails there first. Quality requirements are confirmed in the specification before tender, and sign off records that operations accepted the design.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual packaging and tendering of the sewer rehabilitation program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the ranked rehabilitation projects for the year total about 6 km of lining and 40 manhole renewals.

cards.label: Complete the pre design CCTV and measurements for every reach in the packages so bidders price known conditions
Tender the packages and evaluate the bids on price and on the method statements and past performance
Confirm the funded project list and group the work into tender packages by method, area, and construction season
Award the work and hold the pre construction meeting covering bypass, notification, and quality hold points
Track construction progress and acceptance results and carry lessons into the next year packages
Prepare the specifications with the standard quality, acceptance, and warranty requirements for each method

tasks.explanation: Packages are grouped for constructibility and priced on fresh condition data. Evaluation weighs method and past performance with price, and acceptance lessons improve the next year rather than being relearned.

tasks.prompt: Order a sewer joint grouting program for infiltration at pipe joints.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: CCTV in a high groundwater basin shows infiltration at many joints in otherwise sound pipe, making grouting the proportionate repair.

cards.label: Complete the post grouting CCTV during active groundwater conditions and confirm the treated joints are sealed
Grout the joints under the specified pressures and record the grout take and the test result at each joint
Update the basin infiltration estimate and the asset records with the treated reaches and the results
Select the candidate reaches from CCTV where infiltration is at joints and the pipe structure is otherwise sound
Confirm the groundwater conditions and schedule the work for the high groundwater season when leaks are active and can be proven sealed
Clean the reaches and complete the pre grouting CCTV to map every joint to be treated

tasks.explanation: Grouting only suits sound pipe with joint infiltration, so selection is strict. Work is timed to high groundwater so sealing can be proven under the conditions that caused the problem.

tasks.prompt: Order the leadership response to a sanitary sewer overflow reaching a watercourse.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sewage is overflowing from a manhole beside a creek during a storm and the overall responsible operator is directing the response.

cards.label: Confirm the overflow location, the estimated start time, and that field crews are being dispatched with containment equipment
Direct the cleanup, the removal of visible solids, and the sampling plan for the creek as conditions allow
Complete the overflow record with volumes, times, and actions and open the investigation file before the response stands down
Issue the public notification for the affected watercourse area through the approved communication channel
Notify the supervisor chain, the Spills Action Centre, and the downstream water users as the notification procedure requires
Direct containment at the overflow and at the creek entry points and assign a crew to stop the cause, such as clearing a blockage or restoring pumping

tasks.explanation: Confirmation and containment come first, and notifications run while crews work, not after. The record and the investigation are opened before stand down, while times and volumes can still be established.

tasks.prompt: Order the deployment of bypass pumping for a planned trunk sewer repair.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk section will be isolated for two days and the full flow must be bypassed around the work area.

cards.label: Select the pump arrangement, suction and discharge points, and hose or pipe routes and confirm the discharge can accept the flow
Transfer the flow fully to the bypass, isolate the work section, and confirm the section is safe to open
Prove the bypass by running it under flow while the main line is still available as a fallback
Calculate the bypass capacity needed from the measured dry and wet weather flows and the weather forecast for the work window
Install the bypass with plugs tested and holding, alarms on the suction well, and standby pumps and fuel on site
Monitor levels, fuel, and alarms continuously through the work and restore the main line only after the repair passes its checks

tasks.explanation: Capacity is calculated from measured flows and the forecast, not guessed. The bypass is proven while a fallback still exists, and continuous monitoring protects the whole isolation period.

tasks.prompt: Order the regulatory reporting sequence for a reportable sewage overflow in Ontario.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow from the collection system has occurred and Ontario reporting duties apply under the environmental compliance approval and Regulation 129/04 framework.

cards.label: Record the facts of the event as they are confirmed, including start and stop times, location, cause, estimated volume, and receiving environment
Post the public notice or advisory required by the approval for the affected area
File all notifications and reports in the overflow record and brief the overall responsible operator on the completed duties
Notify the medical officer of health and the downstream drinking water system owners where the procedure requires it for the receiving water
Make the immediate verbal notification to the Spills Action Centre and record the name, time, and the spill reference information given
Submit the written follow up report within the approval timeline with the cause, the actions taken, and the corrective measures

tasks.explanation: Facts are recorded as confirmed so notifications are accurate. Verbal notification is immediate, written follow up is complete and on time, and the filed record proves every duty was met.

tasks.prompt: Order the public notification process for an overflow affecting a recreational water area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow has reached a lake near a public beach during the summer season.

cards.label: Notify the local health unit immediately so beach posting and sampling decisions can be made without delay
Post the notice through the municipal channels and at the affected access points with field staff assistance
Prepare the public notice using the approved wording, stating the location, the advice to avoid contact, and where updates will appear
Confirm with the response lead the affected area, the start time, and whether the overflow is continuing
Update the notice when the overflow stops and again when sampling or the health unit advises the area can reopen
Record every notice, time, and channel in the event file for the regulatory report

tasks.explanation: The health unit is notified before public wording is drafted, because beach decisions are theirs. Notices are updated at each change of state, and the file record supports the regulatory report.

tasks.prompt: Order the post overflow investigation and root cause analysis.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a wet weather overflow occurred at a manhole with no previous overflow history and the cause is not obvious.

cards.label: Preserve the event evidence, including SCADA and level records, rainfall data, crew notes, and photographs, before systems are reset
Issue the corrective actions with owners and dates and enter them into the CMOM improvement tracker
Test the leading cause hypotheses against the timeline and the flow and rainfall records
Confirm the root cause and the contributing factors with operations and engineering review
Inspect the site and the upstream and downstream reaches for blockages, defects, or surcharge evidence
Build the event timeline from the first alarm or report to the confirmed stop of the overflow

tasks.explanation: Evidence is preserved before it is overwritten by normal operations. Hypotheses are tested against the timeline and records, and corrective actions with owners close the investigation.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet weather readiness plan before a forecast major storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a storm with heavy rain is forecast in 48 hours for a system with known wet weather overflow locations.

cards.label: Brief customer service on the expected call types and the information to capture from flooding reports
Confirm the staffing roster, the on call chain, and the mutual aid contacts for the storm period
Monitor the system through the storm from the operations centre and log decisions and deployments as they occur
Check the critical lift stations for fuel, generator readiness, alarm function, and wet well levels drawn down where the procedure allows
Review the forecast and the known surcharge, overflow, and flooding locations and assign each a readiness action
Stage bypass pumps, hoses, vacuum trucks, and barricades at the locations where history says they will be needed

tasks.explanation: History and forecast together decide where equipment is staged. Staffing and customer service are readied before the rain, and live logging during the storm becomes the event record.

tasks.prompt: Order the coordination of a basement flooding response after an extreme storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dozens of basement flooding reports are arriving from one sewershed after a storm that exceeded the design event.

cards.label: Group the reports by street and compare them with the sewer layout to identify the affected reach and any pattern suggesting a blockage rather than general surcharge
Complete the sewershed investigation comparing rainfall, flows, and the system capacity and file the findings
Inspect the affected reach for blockage or damage and clear any obstruction that is adding to the flooding
Report the findings and any capacity or maintenance actions to management and to the affected residents as the procedure requires
Record each property report with times and details in the flooding register for the investigation and any claims process
Advise affected residents through the approved channel on safety, cleanup guidance, and how their report will be investigated

tasks.explanation: Grouping reports by street separates a fixable blockage from general surcharge early. Residents receive safety advice while the investigation proceeds, and the register supports both the engineering findings and any claims.

tasks.prompt: Order the estimation and documentation of an overflow volume.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow ran for several hours from a manhole before it was stopped and a defensible volume is needed for the report.

cards.label: File the calculation, the evidence, and the reviewed estimate in the overflow record
Establish the start and stop times from alarms, level records, crew observations, and the first public report, and note the confidence in each
Calculate the volume with the selected method and state the assumptions and the uncertainty range
Select the estimation method that matches the evidence available and record why it was chosen
Have the estimate reviewed by the supervisor or the overall responsible operator before it enters the report
Determine the overflow rate evidence, such as the depth over the manhole rim, photographs, pump records, or the upstream flow record

tasks.explanation: Times and rate evidence are established before a method is chosen, because the method must fit the evidence. Review before reporting protects the credibility of the number.

tasks.prompt: Order the design of a bypass plan for an emergency force main repair.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a force main has failed and the tributary lift station must be bypassed to a downstream gravity sewer while the main is repaired.

cards.label: Select the bypass route and discharge point and confirm the receiving sewer has capacity for the bypassed flow
Size the bypass pumps and hoses for the peak inflow with a standby pump included
Install and prove the bypass and confirm the station can be held at a safe level before the force main is isolated
Hold the bypass through the repair and the controlled refill of the main and stand it down only after normal pumping is proven
Isolate and drain the failed section and release it to the repair crew with the isolation documented
Confirm the station inflow range and the time available in wet well and upstream storage before an overflow occurs

tasks.explanation: Storage time sets the urgency and the receiving sewer capacity sets the route. The bypass is proven before the main is isolated, and it stays until normal pumping is proven again.

tasks.prompt: Order the environmental cleanup and sampling after an overflow to a ditch and creek.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow has stopped and the affected area includes a roadside ditch flowing to a creek.

cards.label: Collect the water samples at the locations and times set in the sampling plan, including upstream background where required
Remove pooled sewage and visible solids from the ditch by vacuum truck, working from the overflow point downstream
Inspect the creek banks for deposited solids and remove any accumulations found
Record the cleanup actions, the sample results when received, and the area condition in the event file
Apply the cleanup and disinfection steps in the spill procedure to the affected ground and hard surfaces
Confirm the overflow has stopped and the area is safe for cleanup crews, with traffic control where the ditch meets the road

tasks.explanation: Cleanup works downstream from the source so removed material is not replaced by flow from above. Sampling follows the plan rather than convenience, and the event file records both actions and results.

tasks.prompt: Order the activation of mutual aid for a major collection system emergency.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a regional storm has caused multiple overflows and equipment failures beyond the capacity of the on shift staff and fleet.

cards.label: Confirm the scale of the event against the emergency plan thresholds and record the decision to request mutual aid
Contact the mutual aid partners through the established agreements and confirm what each can send and when it will arrive
Assign a liaison and work assignments for the incoming resources and brief them on safety, reporting, and the local procedures
Release the resources as the event allows, complete the cost and event records, and thank the partners through the formal channel
Define the specific help needed, including crews, vacuum trucks, bypass pumps, and generators, with quantities and durations
Track the deployed resources, their tasks, and their hours through the event in the operations log

tasks.explanation: The request is specific, because partners can only send what is asked for. Incoming resources are briefed and tracked like own resources, and formal release and records close the activation properly.

tasks.prompt: Order the after action review following a major overflow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a storm event caused three overflows, a beach posting, and mutual aid activation over two days.

cards.label: Hold the review with operations, communications, and management and build the agreed timeline of decisions and actions
Collect the event records, logs, notifications, and sampling results into a single event file while memories are fresh
Agree the corrective actions and assign each an owner and a completion date
Report the review summary to senior management and track the actions to completion at the quarterly review
Identify what worked, what failed, and what was missing, separating equipment, procedure, staffing, and communication findings
Update the emergency response plan, the CMOM tracker, and any training needs from the agreed actions

tasks.explanation: Records are gathered before the review so it argues from evidence. Findings are converted to owned actions that update the plans, and completion is tracked rather than assumed.

tasks.prompt: Order the build of a collection system asset inventory and registry.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: asset records are scattered across drawings, spreadsheets, and operator knowledge and a single registry is required.

cards.label: Define the asset hierarchy and the attributes each asset class must carry, such as material, size, age, and location
Compile the existing records from drawings, project files, and maintenance history into the registry structure
Assign each asset a unique identifier used by the registry, the work order system, and the mapping system
Set the update procedure so projects and maintenance work return asset changes to the registry as work closes
Field verify a sample of each asset class and correct the attributes that records alone get wrong
Resolve the duplicates, gaps, and conflicts found and record the confidence level for unverified assets

tasks.explanation: The hierarchy and attributes are defined before records are compiled, or the registry inherits every inconsistency. A single identifier across systems and an update procedure keep the registry alive after the build.

tasks.prompt: Order an asset criticality ranking for the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility will rank sewers, manholes, and stations by criticality to drive inspection and renewal priorities.

cards.label: Define the consequence factors for this system, covering public health, environment, road class, customers affected, and repair difficulty
Combine the consequence scores with the likelihood information from condition and failure history where it exists
Score the consequence for each asset or asset group using the agreed scoring guide
Gather the data for each factor from the registry, the mapping system, and operations knowledge
Publish the criticality ranking and set its use in the inspection, cleaning, and capital prioritization procedures
Review the top ranked assets with operations and engineering and correct scores that contradict known field reality

tasks.explanation: Consequence is scored from an agreed guide before likelihood is added, so criticality is not just condition renamed. Field review of the top ranks catches data errors before the ranking drives spending.

tasks.prompt: Order the development of a ten year capital plan for the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the plan must combine renewal, capacity, and compliance projects into a funded ten year program.

cards.label: Assemble the needs from the condition programs, the capacity assessments, the corrosion and infiltration programs, and growth forecasts
Present the plan with the funding profile and the deferred risk to council or the board for approval
Review and refresh the plan annually with new condition and capacity evidence
Fit the ranked needs to the forecast funding by year, deferring the lowest risk work and recording what risk the deferral accepts
Rank the needs by risk and regulatory duty and test the ranking against the criticality results
Cost each need at a planning level and confirm the timing each need becomes critical

tasks.explanation: Needs are assembled from every evidence stream before costing and ranking. Deferral is an explicit risk decision recorded in the plan, and the annual refresh keeps the plan tied to new evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the setting of a level of service framework for collection services.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: council wants measurable service commitments for overflows, flooding protection, response times, and asset condition.

cards.label: Confirm the current performance against each target from the verified historical data
Define a measurable indicator and a target for each outcome that the utility can actually report from its records
Identify the service outcomes the community and the regulator expect, from the approval requirements and past council direction
Report performance against the adopted targets annually and bring forward the actions where targets are missed
Present the framework, the current performance, and the costed gaps for council adoption
Cost the changes in programs or capital needed where current performance misses a target

tasks.explanation: Indicators must be measurable from real records before targets are promised. Current performance is established honestly, gaps are costed, and annual reporting closes the accountability loop.

tasks.prompt: Order a lifecycle cost comparison for a sewer renewal decision.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a deteriorated reach can be lined for a shorter life extension or replaced for a longer life at higher cost.

cards.label: Recommend the option with the reasoning recorded, including any non cost factors such as disruption or capacity
File the analysis with the project record so the decision can be revisited when the asset is next assessed
Define the options and the analysis period and list the costs each option carries, including construction, maintenance, and future renewal
Calculate the total lifecycle cost of each option over the analysis period using the municipal discount and escalation guidance
Estimate the service life of each option from the condition evidence and the performance record of the methods in this system
Test the comparison for sensitivity to the life estimates and to the construction costs

tasks.explanation: Options, lives, and costs are defined before any total is calculated. Sensitivity testing shows whether the answer survives honest uncertainty, and the filed analysis makes the decision auditable.

tasks.prompt: Order a risk based renewal prioritization for the annual capital program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: candidate renewal projects exceed the annual budget by three times and must be ranked by risk.

cards.label: Confirm each candidate has current condition evidence and a consequence assessment, and return incomplete candidates for assessment first
Select the program that fits the budget from the top of the adjusted ranking and record the risk carried by the deferred projects
Calculate the risk for each candidate from the likelihood of failure and the consequence of failure scores
Adjust the ranking for projects where failure would breach a regulatory duty or affect a critical customer such as a hospital
Carry the deferred projects forward with updated condition checks so their risk is refreshed for the next year
Present the selected program and the deferred risk statement for approval

tasks.explanation: Candidates without current evidence are assessed before they compete for money. Deferred risk is stated openly at approval, and deferred projects are rechecked rather than forgotten.

tasks.prompt: Order the funding approval sequence for a major collection capital project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk sewer renewal estimated in the multi million range requires council approval and a funding plan.

cards.label: Prepare the business case showing the cost of deferral and the service and compliance consequences
Report project progress, spending, and any scope change back through the capital reporting process
Present the project through the budget process and record the approval conditions council attaches
Complete the project definition with scope, cost estimate class, schedule, and the risk the project retires
Enter the approved project into the capital plan with its cash flow by year and its project manager assigned
Confirm the funding sources, covering reserves, development charges where eligible, debenture, and any grant programs

tasks.explanation: Definition and funding sources precede the business case, because approval without identified funding is not a plan. Conditions attached at approval are recorded and progress is reported against them.

tasks.prompt: Order an asset data quality improvement program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an audit found missing ages, wrong materials, and duplicate records in about a fifth of the registry.

cards.label: Set the correction priorities where bad data affects decisions, such as criticality ranking and renewal selection
Correct the priority records using project files and field verification for the attributes that cannot be resolved from records
Remeasure data quality after a year and report the improvement and the remaining gaps
Fix the entry procedures and validation checks that allowed the errors, including pick lists and required fields
Measure the data quality by field and by asset class so the worst gaps are known rather than assumed
Train the staff who create and update asset records on the corrected procedures

tasks.explanation: Quality is measured before it is fixed, and corrections are prioritized by the decisions the data drives. Fixing entry procedures matters as much as fixing records, or the errors return.

tasks.prompt: Order the condition update cycle for the collection asset base.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility will keep condition current on a rolling cycle so no sewer or structure exceeds its inspection interval.

cards.label: Set the inspection interval for each asset class from its criticality and deterioration rate
Report the percentage of the asset base within its inspection interval as a CMOM indicator
Build the rolling schedule from the last inspection dates so the most overdue and most critical assets come first
Deliver the inspections to the standard grading and load the results into the registry as they are completed
Feed the changed condition picture into the renewal prioritization and the capital plan refresh
Recalculate the condition distribution of the asset base and compare it with the previous cycle

tasks.explanation: Intervals follow criticality and deterioration, not a single blanket cycle. Results flow into renewal decisions each cycle, and the currency indicator shows whether the program is keeping up.

tasks.prompt: Order the capacity capital planning for system growth areas.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: official plan growth will add major flows to two trunk sewers and three lift stations over fifteen years.

cards.label: Review the plan whenever the growth forecast or the phasing changes and adjust the triggers
Identify the upgrades each phase requires and the latest date each must be in service
Confirm the growth areas, the phasing, and the design flows with the planning department and the development forecast
Sequence the upgrades with the development phasing and the funding sources, including development charges where eligible
Assess the current capacity and condition of the affected trunks and stations against the phased flows
Enter the sequenced upgrades into the capital plan with triggers tied to development approvals

tasks.explanation: Growth flows and phasing come from the planning source before capacity is judged. Upgrades are sequenced to be in service when the flows arrive, with triggers that move when the forecast moves.

tasks.prompt: Order the designation and coverage schedule for the overall responsible operator.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the Class 3 collection system must have a designated overall responsible operator at all times under Ontario Regulation 129/04.

cards.label: Build the coverage schedule so a designated operator is assigned for every operating period, including nights, weekends, and vacations
Set the handover procedure so the outgoing and incoming designated operators exchange active issues and open regulatory duties
Designate the overall responsible operator and the alternates in writing with the effective dates and the scope of the designation
Communicate the schedule and the contact route to all operators, the monitoring point, and management
Confirm the operators who hold the required licence class and experience to act as overall responsible operator for this system
Review the designations after any staffing or licence change and reissue the schedule when a designation changes

tasks.explanation: Eligibility is confirmed before designation, and designation is written before scheduling. Handover and review after staffing changes keep continuous coverage real rather than nominal.

tasks.prompt: Order an operator certification and training compliance review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the annual review must confirm every operator licence, training hours, and certification duty for the collection system is current.

cards.label: File the review and report the compliance status and the open gaps to management
Compare the records against the Regulation 129/04 requirements for the system class and the duties each operator performs
Confirm the overall responsible operator designations still match the licences held after any change
Arrange the courses, exam sittings, and supervised experience needed to close each gap before its date
Compile the licence status, expiry dates, and training records for every operator and operator in training
Identify any licence, training hour, or renewal gap and the date it becomes a compliance problem

tasks.explanation: Records are compared against the actual requirements for the duties performed, not just collected. Gaps are closed before their dates, and designations are rechecked because they depend on the licences reviewed.

tasks.prompt: Order the supervisory command of a major collection emergency using an incident structure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk sewer collapse has closed a major road, caused an overflow, and requires multiple crews, contractors, and city departments.

cards.label: Brief all responding groups on the objectives, the hazards, and the reporting chain before work expands
Establish the incident command, name the incident lead, and assign the operations, logistics, communications, and safety roles
Coordinate the external communications, the regulator notifications, and the elected official briefings through the assigned roles
Close the incident with a documented demobilization and open the after action review file
Set the incident objectives for the first operating period, covering public safety, overflow control, and road and utility protection
Direct the work in operating periods with a situation report and revised objectives at the end of each period

tasks.explanation: Command and roles are established before objectives are set, and objectives before work expands. Period by period direction keeps a multi agency response coherent, and demobilization hands off to the review.

tasks.prompt: Order the onboarding of a new collection operations supervisor.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a newly promoted supervisor will lead a crew of six operators across cleaning, inspection, and station work.

cards.label: Observe the supervisor running a crew briefing, a work assignment, and an incident response and give documented feedback
Confirm the supervisor licence, the system procedures, and the records the role is accountable for before the start date
Review the live work backlog, the open corrective actions, and the regulatory calendar together and transfer ownership item by item
Confirm the supervisor is carrying the role independently and close the onboarding record with any remaining development actions
Walk the critical stations, overflow locations, and confined space and bypass equipment with the supervisor and the area operators
Pair the supervisor with an experienced supervisor for the first operating cycles, including rounds, work order review, and on call duty

tasks.explanation: Accountability is defined before shadowing begins. Ownership of live work is transferred item by item, observed performance is fed back, and independence is confirmed rather than assumed.

tasks.prompt: Order the performance review of a contracted CCTV and cleaning service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a contractor delivers most of the CCTV and cleaning program and the annual review decides whether the contract is performing.

cards.label: Audit a sample of the delivered CCTV files against the coding standard and the delivered cleaning records against the work orders
Reaudit after the corrective period and record whether the contract returns to full performance or proceeds to retender planning
Compare the measured performance with the contract requirements and list every shortfall with its evidence
Compile the contract measures, including kilometres completed, coding quality results, reinspection findings, and response times
Meet the contractor with the findings and agree the corrective actions and dates in writing
Apply the contract remedies for any shortfall the agreement reserves, such as reinspection at the contractor cost

tasks.explanation: Performance is measured and audited from the delivered files before the contractor is confronted. Corrective actions are written and reaudit decides the contract future on evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order a health and safety program review for confined space work in the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the annual review covers entries into manholes, wet wells, and valve chambers by own crews and contractors.

cards.label: Correct the procedure, training, or equipment gaps found and assign each correction an owner and a date
Report the review to the joint health and safety committee and track the corrections to completion
Compile the year of entry records, incidents, near misses, and equipment inspection and calibration records
Compare the entry procedures and permits against the confined space regulation requirements and the program standard
Observe a planned entry and assess the crew practice against the procedure, including atmospheric testing and attendant duties
Inspect a sample of entry equipment, gas monitors, and rescue equipment for condition and testing currency
